mainTopic: Zevachim 115b: exemptions for offering outside the עזרה, and how קרבנות worked before the משכן was set up.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion with a rule of רב הונא in the name of רב: an אשם that was sent out to graze and then slaughtered without a stated purpose is valid as an עולה. Next, a ברייתא explains why offering up outside the עזרה things that are eaten, like the meat of a חטאת or the שתי הלחם, carries no liability. The word 'עולה' teaches that only what is fit for the מזבח counts. Services that do not finish the עבודה, like pouring, mixing or קבלה, are also exempt, because העלאה is the finishing step. The גמרא then turns to the time before the משכן. רב חסדא says the firstborn served only once at סיני and that the desert עולה needed no skinning and cutting, and a ברייתא contradicts both claims. Each contradiction is answered as a מחלוקת תנאים. The first is רבי יהושע בן קרחה against רבי, which leads to the story of נדב and אביהוא and the praise of אהרן's silence. The second is רבי ישמעאל against רבי עקיבא. Finally, רב הונא learns from נח's offering that domestic animals, wild animals and birds could all be offered before the משכן.

steps.title: רב הונא's rule: a sidelined guilt offering is valid as a burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up the previous point with a rule from רב הונא in the name of רב: an אשם that was sent out to graze and then slaughtered without a stated purpose is valid as an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רב הונא in the name of רב, who said: an אשם that was sent out to graze, and someone slaughtered it without saying what it was for, is valid as an עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the discussion just before this by saying it matches a known rule of רב הונא in the name of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם whose owner no longer needs it is sent out to graze. Once that happens, it stops being treated as an אשם. So if someone slaughters it without naming a purpose, it counts as a valid עולה, and the earlier point rests on this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Sent out to graze, because it is no longer used as its original offering

phrases.english: This is like what Rav Huna said in the name of Rav.
For Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
A guilt offering that was sent out to graze,
phrases.notes: This happens when its owner no longer needs it, so it grazes until it gets a blemish.

phrases.english: and someone slaughtered it without specifying what it was for,
it is valid as a burnt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion that came before this section by grounding it in רב הונא's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Grounding in an accepted אמורא's ruling
steps.terutzMaskana: An אשם that was sent out to graze and then slaughtered without a stated purpose is a valid עולה.

steps.title: Source for exemption when offering up eaten portions outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. A ברייתא then asks for the source that offering up meat or bread meant to be eaten, outside the עזרה, carries no liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One who offers up from the meat of a חטאת, etc.' The Rabbis taught: From where do we know that one who offers up, outside, from the meat of a חטאת, an אשם, קדשי קדשים, קדשים קלים, מותר העומר, שתי הלחם, לחם הפנים, or שירי מנחות is exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה. It brings a ברייתא that asks for the source of the exemption, and this question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every item on the list is eaten by the כהנים or the owners. None of it is burned on the מזבח. The question is where the Torah shows that 'offering up' such things outside is not the forbidden act of offering outside.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of the most holy level
Offerings of a lesser holy level
The leftover of the omer meal offering, which the כהנים eat
What is left of a meal offering after the handful is burned

phrases.english: One who offers up from the meat of a sin offering, etc.
The Rabbis taught:
From where do we know that one who offers up from the meat of a sin offering,
or from the meat of a guilt offering,
or from the meat of the most holy offerings,
or from the meat of offerings of lesser holiness,
or from the leftover of the omer offering,
or the two loaves, or the showbread,
or the leftovers of meal offerings, that he is exempt?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק source showing that offering up eaten portions outside is exempt.

steps.title: Only what is fit for the altar makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the word 'עולה': just as an עולה is fit to go up on the מזבח, only things fit to go up on the מזבח make one liable for offering outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'עולה.' Just as an עולה is fit to be offered on the מזבח, so too only things fit to be offered on the מזבח are included.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question with the word 'עולה' in the פסוק about offering outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah used the example of an עולה, which is burned on the מזבח. From this we learn that liability applies only to things that belong on the מזבח. Meat and bread that are meant to be eaten are left out, so offering them up outside is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit to be offered up on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: Offering up outside makes one liable only for something that is fit for the מזבח, like an עולה. Portions that are meant to be eaten are exempt.

phrases.english: The verse says: "burnt offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:8

phrases.english: just as a burnt offering is fit to be offered up on the altar,
so too, only whatever is fit to be offered up is included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'עולה' limits liability to things that are fit for the מזבח.

steps.title: Source for exemption for preparation services done outside
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks a new question: where do we learn that doing other services outside, ones that are not burning, is also exempt?
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that even one who pours oil, mixes, breaks into pieces, salts, waves, brings near, arranges the שולחן, cleans the lamps, takes the קמיצה, or receives the blood, outside, is exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to a second question about services that are not burning on the מזבח. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 dealt with the kind of item being offered. This question is about the kind of act being done. All these acts are real services in the מקדש, but none of them is the act of offering up on the מזבח. The ברייתא wants a source showing they are exempt when done outside.

keyTerms.meaning: Pours oil onto a meal offering
Mixes the oil into the flour
Brings the meal offering near to the corner of the מזבח
Cleans out the lamps of the מנורה
Takes the handful from a meal offering

phrases.english: From where do we know that even one who pours oil,
and one who mixes, and one who breaks into pieces,
and one who salts, and one who waves,
and one who brings near, and one who arranges the table,
phrases.notes: The table here is the שולחן that holds the showbread.

phrases.english: and one who cleans out the lamps,
and one who takes a handful, and one who receives the blood, outside, that he is exempt?
phrases.notes: 'Outside' applies to the whole list: each act is done outside the עזרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from which items are included to which acts are included.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that services which are not offering up, done outside, are exempt.

steps.title: Only a final step of the service brings liability
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the word 'יעלה' that only a service which finishes the עבודה, like burning, makes one liable when done outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'who offers up an עולה or a זבח.' Just as offering up is the last step of the service, so too only a service that is the last step makes one liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from Step 4. Services done outside that are not the final step of the עבודה are exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The model is הַעֲלָאָה, burning on the מזבח, which is the finishing step of a קרבן. Only a service with that same quality brings liability outside. A service that still has other steps after it is not like העלאה, so it is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Offering up, meaning burning on the מזבח
The finishing step of the service

steps.whatToRemember: Liability for offering outside applies only to a service that finishes the עבודה, modeled on העלאה.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"That offers up a burnt offering or a sacrifice"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:8

phrases.english: Just as offering up is the finishing of the service,
so too, anything that is the finishing of a service.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: אֲשֶׁר יַעֲלֶה עוֹלָה אוֹ זָבַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'יעלה': like העלאה, only a service that finishes the עבודה brings liability outside.

steps.title: The firstborn served once and then stopped
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the time before the משכן. רב חסדא tells רב הונא בר רב קטינא in the name of רבי אסי that the firstborn offered at סיני and then stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Before the משכן was set up, etc.' רב הונא בר רב קטינא was reading the פסוק 'And he sent the young men of בני ישראל.' רב חסדא said to him that רבי אסי said: they offered and then stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. It tells a story where רב חסדא says the firstborn served only at סיני and not afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'young men' in the פסוק are the firstborn, who brought the offerings at מתן תורה. רבי אסי says that was a one-time event: they served that day and then stopped. This sets up a clash with the משנה, which says the firstborn served until the משכן was set up.

keyTerms.meaning: Before the משכן was set up
The young men of Israel, meaning the firstborn

phrases.english: "Until the Tabernacle was set up, etc."
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה. The 'etc.' in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב הוּנָא בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Rav Ketina was sitting
before Rav Chisda,
and he was reading:
"And he sent the young men of the children of Israel."
phrases.notes: שמות 24:5. These young men were the firstborn, who brought offerings at סיני.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rabbi Asi said:
They offered, and then they stopped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אסי, the firstborn performed the service at סיני and then stopped.

steps.title: A second statement: the desert עולה needed no skinning
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא wanted to challenge רב חסדא from the משנה. Then he heard רב חסדא also say that the desert עולה needed no skinning or cutting, so he challenged him from a ברייתא that covers both statements.
steps.simpleTranslation: He thought to challenge him from our משנה. Then he heard him say in the name of רב אדא בר אהבה: the עולה that Israel offered in the desert did not need skinning and cutting up. So he challenged him from a ברייתא that works against both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second statement of רב חסדא and is setting up a challenge. The challenge itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה alone could challenge only the first statement about the firstborn. Once רב חסדא added a second statement, רב הונא picked a ברייתא that can challenge both at once. That is better than using the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Skinning the animal and cutting it into pieces
That works equally against all of them

phrases.english: He thought to challenge him from our mishna;
then he heard him saying
in the name of Rav Adda bar Ahava:
The burnt offering that Israel offered in the wilderness
did not require skinning and cutting into pieces;
so he challenged him from a baraita
that applies equally to all of them.
phrases.notes: One ברייתא that can challenge both of רב חסדא's statements.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second statement by רב חסדא and sets up a challenge to both
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב אדא בר אהבה, the עולה offered in the desert before the משכן did not need skinning and cutting.

steps.title: The ברייתא: before the משכן the firstborn served
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that before the משכן, private altars were allowed, the firstborn did the service, and almost any kosher animal or bird could be offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: Before the משכן was set up, private altars were allowed, the service was done by the firstborn, and everything was fit to be offered: domestic animals, wild animals, and birds; males and females; unblemished and blemished animals. Kosher species, but not non-kosher ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that רב הונא used to challenge רב חסדא. This part shows the firstborn served for the whole time until the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אסי said the firstborn served once at סיני and stopped. This ברייתא says the service was by the firstborn for the whole time before the משכן, which contradicts him. The ברייתא also lists which animals were allowed then: almost all kinds, as long as they were kosher.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'טהורין' and 'טמאין' mean kosher and non-kosher species, not ritually pure and impure animals.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
Until the Tabernacle was set up,
private altars were permitted,
and the service was done by the firstborn,
and everything was fit to be offered:
a domesticated animal, a wild animal, and a bird;
males and females;
unblemished and blemished;
kosher species, but not non-kosher ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the text of the ברייתא announced in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אסי's statement, quoted by רב חסדא, that the firstborn offered and then stopped
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the service was by the firstborn the whole time until the משכן, not just one day at סיני.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא: the desert burnt offering needed skinning and cutting
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying that all offerings before the משכן were עולות, that the desert עולה needed הפשט and ניתוח, and that non-Jews today may bring offerings this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: And everything was offered as burnt offerings. And the burnt offering that the Jewish people offered in the desert needed skinning and cutting into pieces. And non-Jews today are allowed to do this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא that challenges רב חסדא. This last part clashes directly with his second statement about skinning and cutting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said the desert עולה needed no הפשט or ניתוח, but this ברייתא says it did. Together with the earlier line that the firstborn served until the משכן, the ברייתא now contradicts both of his statements.

keyTerms.meaning: Cutting the animal into its pieces
Burnt offerings, which are burned completely on the מזבח

phrases.english: And everything was offered as burnt offerings.
And the burnt offering that the Jewish people offered in the desert
phrases.notes: This means the desert before the משכן was built.

phrases.english: needed skinning and cutting into pieces.
And non-Jews nowadays
are allowed to do so.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹלָה שֶׁהִקְרִיבוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּמִּדְבָּר טְעוּנָה הֶפְשֵׁט וְנִיתּוּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's statements that the firstborn stopped serving at סיני and that the desert עולה needed no skinning or cutting
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says outright that the firstborn served until the משכן and that the desert עולה needed הפשט and ניתוח, which contradicts both statements.

steps.title: It is a מחלוקת תנאים about who the כהנים at סיני were
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that this is a מחלוקת תנאים. רבי יהושע בן קרחה says the כהנים warned at סיני were the firstborn, while רבי says they were נדב and אביהוא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים. As it was taught: 'And also the כהנים who come near to ה׳ shall make themselves holy.' רבי יהושע בן קרחה says: this is the separation of the firstborn. רבי says: this is the separation of נדב and אביהוא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא defends himself. He says the ברייתא follows one תנא, and he follows another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At סיני, God warned 'the כהנים' to keep back. If those כהנים were the firstborn, the firstborn were still serving, as the ברייתא says. רבי says they were נדב and אביהוא, so the firstborn had already stopped serving at סיני, which fits רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
Separation, being told to keep back
The two older sons of אהרן

steps.confusionAlert: This answer only deals with the firstborn part of the challenge. It does not yet explain the skinning and cutting.

phrases.english: It is a dispute between תנאים;
as it was taught in a ברייתא:
'And also the כהנים who come near to Hashem shall make themselves holy'
phrases.notes: שמות 19:22

phrases.english: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says:
This is the separation of the firstborn.
רבי says:
This is the separation of נדב and אביהוא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: מחלוקת תנאים: the ברייתא follows one תנא, and רב חסדא follows the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to disprove רב חסדא's claim about the firstborn.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב חסדא follows רבי, who holds that the כהנים at סיני were נדב and אביהוא, so the firstborn had already stopped serving.

steps.title: Where does the firstborn opinion find a hint about נדב and אביהוא?
steps.stepSummary: For רבי, the warning at סיני explains משה's words 'this is what ה׳ spoke' after נדב and אביהוא died. The גמרא asks where רבי יהושע בן קרחה finds such a hint.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who says it is the separation of נדב and אביהוא. That is why it is written: 'This is what ה׳ spoke, saying: through those close to Me I will be made holy.' But for the one who says it is the separation of the firstborn, where is it hinted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question on רבי יהושע בן קרחה's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After נדב and אביהוא died, משה said 'this is what ה׳ spoke.' That means God had said it earlier. For רבי, God said it at סיני, when He warned those כהנים. For רבי יהושע בן קרחה, that warning was about the firstborn, so where did God ever say it?

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for, it makes sense for
That is why it is written
Through those close to Me I will be made holy

phrases.english: It works well for the one who says
this is the separation of נדב and אביהוא:
that is why it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״הוּא אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר ה׳ לֵאמֹר בִּקְרֹבַי אֶקָּדֵשׁ״.
phrases.english: 'This is what ה׳ spoke, saying: through those close to Me I will be made holy.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:3. משה says this to אהרן right after נדב and אביהוא died.

phrases.english: But for the one who says
this is the separation of the firstborn,
where is it hinted?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר זוֹ פְּרִישׁוּת נָדָב וַאֲבִיהוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about one side of the מחלוקת quoted in step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where, according to רבי יהושע בן קרחה, did God earlier say He would be made holy through נדב and אביהוא?

steps.title: The hint is in ונקדש בכבודי, read as 'My honored ones'
steps.stepSummary: The hint is in the פסוק 'ונקדש בכבודי.' Do not read it as 'by My glory.' Read it as 'by My honored ones,' meaning נדב and אביהוא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And I will meet there with the Jewish people, and it will be made holy by My glory.' Do not read it 'by My glory'; rather, read it 'by My honored ones.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that God already hinted it when He spoke about the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the משכן says it will be made holy 'בכבודי.' The גמרא reads this word as 'My honored ones.' So God hinted that the משכן would be made holy through His honored ones, נדב and אביהוא. This gives רבי יהושע בן קרחה a source for משה's words.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read it as, a way of reading the word differently to learn something

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי, the warning at סיני to 'the כהנים' was about נדב and אביהוא, so the firstborn had already stopped serving, as רב חסדא said. For רבי יהושע בן קרחה, the warning was about the firstborn, and the hint about נדב and אביהוא comes from ונקדש בכבודי, read as 'by My honored ones.'

phrases.english: As it is written:
'And I will meet there with the Jewish people, and it will be made holy by My glory.'
phrases.notes: שמות 29:43

phrases.english: Do not read it 'by My glory,'
rather, read it 'by My honored ones.'
phrases.notes: The standard printed גמרא has the word in round brackets, and the corrected wording is the one in square brackets. Both mean 'My honored ones.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: God hinted it in ונקדש בכבודי, read as 'by My honored ones,' meaning נדב and אביהוא.

steps.title: משה explains to אהרן why his sons died, and אהרן stays silent
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ told משה 'ונקדש בכבודי,' but משה only understood it when נדב and אביהוא died. He told אהרן that his sons died to sanctify ה׳'s name. אהרן then stayed silent and was rewarded.
steps.simpleTranslation: ה׳ told משה this statement, but its meaning was not understood until אהרן's sons died. Then משה said: 'אהרן, my brother, your sons died only to sanctify ה׳'s name.' When אהרן realized his sons were close to ה׳, he was silent and got reward, as it says 'And אהרן was silent.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the explanation from Step 12 and tells what משה said to אהרן after his sons died. It also tells how אהרן reacted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 12, 'בכבודי' was read as 'My honored ones,' meaning נדב and אביהוא. Now we learn that משה had heard this message earlier but only understood it when they died. אהרן's silence is praised as a deliberate act that earned reward.

keyTerms.meaning: Close to ה׳ (literally 'known to the Place'; מקום is a name for ה׳)

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר זֶה אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה
phrases.english: This matter the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moshe

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יָדְעוּ, עַד שֶׁמֵּתוּ בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן.
phrases.english: but they did not know it, until the sons of Aharon died.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁמֵּתוּ בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן, אָמַר לוֹ:
phrases.english: Once the sons of Aharon died, he said to him:
Aharon, my brother, your sons did not die

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְהַקְדִּישׁ שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא.
phrases.english: except to sanctify the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He.
Once Aharon knew
that his sons were close to the Omnipresent,
he was silent and received reward;
as it is said: 'And Aharon was silent.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:3

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר זֶה אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the reading of 'ונקדש בכבודי' from Step 12 and explains what משה told אהרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נדב and אביהוא died to sanctify ה׳'s name, and אהרן was rewarded for accepting this in silence.

steps.title: פסוקים from דוד and שלמה about the value of silence
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings two more פסוקים that praise silence: דוד's 'דום לה׳' and שלמה's 'עת לחשות ועת לדבר.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, דוד says: 'Be silent before ה׳ and wait for Him.' Even if He strikes down many dead around you, stay silent. Similarly, שלמה says: 'A time to be silent and a time to speak.' Sometimes a person is silent and gets reward for the silence, and sometimes a person speaks and gets reward for the speaking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the idea that אהרן's silence earned reward. It brings similar פסוקים from דוד and שלמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד's 'דום' matches the word 'וידום' used for אהרן. 'והתחולל' is read as hinting at חללים, people killed. So even when tragedy strikes, a person should accept it quietly. שלמה adds that silence is not always right: sometimes speaking also earns reward.

phrases.english: And likewise regarding David it says:
'Be silent before ה׳ and wait for Him' —
phrases.notes: תהלים 37:7. The word והתחולל is being read as a hint to חללים, the dead.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמַּפִּיל לְךָ חֲלָלִים חֲלָלִים,
phrases.english: even though He strikes down many dead around you,
you be silent.
And likewise regarding Shlomo it says:
'A time to be silent and a time to speak' —
phrases.notes: קהלת 3:7

phrases.english: sometimes one is silent
and receives reward for the silence,
sometimes one speaks
and receives reward for the speech.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 13's point that אהרן's silence earned reward.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that accepting ה׳'s judgment in silence is praiseworthy and rewarded.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן‎: ה׳ is feared when He judges His holy ones
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads 'ממקדשך' as 'ממקודשיך,' 'from Your holy ones.' When ה׳ judges His holy ones, He becomes feared and praised. This fits the death of נדב and אביהוא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What does the פסוק 'Awesome is God from Your holy places' mean? Don't read it as 'from Your holy places,' but as 'from Your holy ones.' When ה׳ judges His holy ones, He is feared, exalted, and praised.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן teaches the same idea. When ה׳ punishes the people closest to Him, His name becomes sanctified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another 'אל תקרי' reading, like the reading of 'בכבודי' in Step 12. The phrase 'His holy ones' fits נדב and אביהוא. רבי יוחנן's teaching backs up the idea from Step 13 that ה׳'s name is made holy when He judges those closest to Him. It is not another hint for רבי יהושע בן קרחה; his hint was already given in Step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what (someone else) said; it shows the same idea
Do not read it as, a way of reading a word differently

steps.whatToRemember: With this, the first contradiction from the ברייתא is settled. Whether the בכורות served before the משכן depends on the מחלוקת תנאים between רבי יהושע בן קרחה and רבי.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
What is meant by what is written: 'Awesome is God from Your holy places'?
phrases.notes: תהלים 68:36

phrases.english: Do not read it as 'from Your holy places'
but rather 'from Your holy ones' —
at the time that the Holy One, Blessed be He, carries out
judgment upon His holy ones,
He is feared, and exalted, and praised.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside teaching that matches the idea from Steps 12–13 and closes that branch.
steps.raayaObject: ה׳'s name is sanctified when He judges those closest to Him, as with נדב and אביהוא.

steps.title: The problem of the desert burnt offering still remains
steps.stepSummary: The first problem is settled, but the second part of the ברייתא is still difficult. It said the desert עולה needed הפשט and ניתוח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the burnt offering is still a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second problem from the ברייתא. It says the issue about the עולה has not been answered yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 only explained the contradiction about who did the service, the בכורות. The ברייתא in Step 9 also said that the עולה brought in the desert needed הפשט and ניתוח. That still conflicts with the earlier view that it did not need them.

keyTerms.meaning: Skinning the animal and cutting it into pieces

phrases.english: But the burnt offering is still a difficulty!
phrases.notes: Back to Step 9: the ברייתא said the desert עולה needed skinning and cutting, which goes against the earlier view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the בכורות issue is settled, the גמרא goes back to the second contradiction raised in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the עולה brought in the desert did not need הפשט and ניתוח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the desert עולה did need הפשט and ניתוח, and Step 10 did not resolve this.

steps.title: This too is a dispute between two תנאים, starting with רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the עולה question is also a מחלוקת תנאים. רבי ישמעאל says only general rules were given at סיני, and the details came in the אהל מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between two תנאים. As it is taught: רבי ישמעאל says, general rules were said at סיני, and the details were said in the Tent of Meeting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the עולה problem the same way it answered the בכורות problem: the sources reflect two different תנאים. It begins by quoting the first one, רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי ישמעאל, detailed laws, such as skinning and cutting the עולה, were taught only in the אהל מועד, after the משכן was built. So the עולה brought at סיני did not need them. The ברייתא that says it did must follow a different תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: Two תנאים, meaning two sages who disagree

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי ישמעאל means the details were unknown forever. He means they were taught later, in the אהל מועד, so they did not apply yet at סיני.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of two tannaim;
as it is taught: Rabbi Yishmael says:
general rules were said at Sinai,
and details in the Tent of Meeting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מחלוקת תנאים: the conflicting sources follow different sages
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All sources agree about the desert עולה, so the ברייתא contradicts the other view.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי ישמעאל, the details such as הפשט and ניתוח were given only in the אהל מועד, so the desert עולה did not need them. The ברייתא follows a different תנא.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: details were given at סיני too
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds that both the general rules and the details were said at סיני. They were taught again in the אהל מועד and a third time in ערבות מואב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: the general rules and the details were all said at סיני. They were repeated in the אהל מועד and taught a third time in the plains of מואב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the מחלוקת from the last step. רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל said only general rules came at סיני. רבי עקיבא says the details came at סיני too. So according to רבי עקיבא, the details of the עולה, like הפשט and ניתוח, were already known in the desert. The ברייתא that seemed difficult follows רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: The plains of מואב, where משה reviewed the תורה before he died

steps.whatToRemember: The question about the desert עולה is solved: the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, who holds the details were already given at סיני.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
General rules and details were said at Sinai,
and they were taught again in the Tent of Meeting,
and they were taught a third time in the plains of Moab.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: כְּלָלוֹת וּפְרָטוֹת נֶאֶמְרוּ בְּסִינַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the מחלוקת תנאים that began with רבי ישמעאל in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to one side of a מחלוקת תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed the desert עולה could not have needed הפשט and ניתוח, since those details came later.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי עקיבא, the details were given at סיני, so the desert עולה already needed הפשט and ניתוח.

steps.title: Where do we learn that every kind could be offered?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another line of the ברייתא: 'all are fit to be offered.' It asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said in the ברייתא: 'All are fit to be offered.' Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting another line from the ברייתא. It is setting up the next step, where a source will be given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that before the משכן went up, every kind of animal and bird could be brought. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit to be brought as a קרבן
From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: The Master said:
All are fit to be offered.
phrases.notes: This is from the ברייתא from earlier: before the משכן, domestic animals, wild animals and birds could all be offered.

phrases.english: From where are these words learned?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁירִין לְהַקְרִיב. מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of סיני and the עולה, and turns to another line of the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches that all kinds of animals and birds could be offered before the משכן.

steps.title: רב הונא learns it from נח's offering
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא quotes the פסוק where נח took from every pure animal and every pure bird. 'Animal' means a domestic animal, and a wild animal is included in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: the פסוק says, 'And נח built a מזבח to ה׳, and took of every pure animal and of every pure bird.' 'Animal' means what it sounds like, a domestic animal. A wild animal (חיה) is also included in the word 'animal.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question with a פסוק about נח's offering after the flood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names animals and birds, so those are clearly allowed. The word בהמה is read in its plain meaning, a domestic animal. But חיה, a wild animal, also counts as part of בהמה, so it was allowed too. That covers all three kinds: domestic animals, wild animals and birds.

keyTerms.meaning: A domestic animal, like a cow or sheep
A wild animal, like a deer
In its plain meaning, as it sounds

steps.whatToRemember: Before the משכן, domestic animals, wild animals and birds could all be offered. We learn it from נח, and חיה is included in the word בהמה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think חיה is left out because the פסוק only says בהמה. The גמרא says חיה is included inside the word בהמה.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
As the verse says:
"And Noah built an altar to ה׳,
phrases.notes: בראשית 8:20

phrases.english: and took of every pure animal
and of every pure bird";
"Animal" means what it sounds like.
phrases.notes: He means a regular domestic animal, like a cow or a sheep.

phrases.english: A wild animal is included in "animal."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, דְּאָמַר קְרָא: וַיִּבֶן נֹחַ מִזְבֵּחַ לַה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק of נח's offering shows that animals and birds could be offered, and חיה is included in בהמה.
